title: Move md5 passwords onto password_hash
summary: Migrate users that cannot be rehashed in bulk, one login at a time.

files.content:
<?php

final class Auth
{
    public function __construct(private readonly PDO $pdo)
    {
    }

    public function register(string $email, string $password): void
    {
        $stmt = $this->pdo->prepare('INSERT INTO users (email, password) VALUES (?, ?)');
        $stmt->execute([$email, md5($password)]);
    }

    public function login(string $email, string $password): bool
    {
        $row = $this->findByEmail($email);

        return $row !== false && $row['password'] === md5($password);
    }
}

turns.user: audit flagged md5 passwords. move to password_hash. we have ~400k users so no big bang rewrite

assistant.body: One pass over 400k rows is off the table, so the migration rides on login. register gets password_hash right away, and login rewrites the row the moment an old md5 verifies. No md5 survives a successful login.

turns.user: you're keying off $2y$ - doesn't that break every new account the day php flips the default to argon2?

assistant.body: Good catch. Sniffing the prefix breaks the day the default moves. Treating a 32 character hex string as the only legacy shape hands everything else to password_verify, which keeps up with whatever PHP picks.

turns.user: also an unknown email comes back way faster than a real one. that's enumerable isn't it

assistant.body: A missing row now costs what a real one costs: verify against a throwaway hash, then return false. The address stops showing up in the timing.

turns.user: login api got slow, people are complaining. cost 12 is too much, go with 11. same for the migrated ones

assistant.body: Pinning the cost at 11 rather than leaving it to the default. Both call sites need the same options array, register and rehash, so one substitution covers them.

turns.user: sorry, forgot one. the batch we imported years ago stores md5 in uppercase. pick those up too

assistant.body: Widening the legacy test to uppercase and folding the stored value down before the compare. md5 only ever emits lowercase, so normalising the stored side covers both spellings.
